E01 y E02 no tienen (E01 tiene su cutscene). Frames: image (images/newsreel/<image>.png), lower_third, caption, seconds, audio, variants, if, classified.

frames.caption: Good evening. At seven o'clock tonight the President spoke to the nation from the White House. For most Americans, it was the first they had heard of missiles in Cuba.
"It shall be the policy of this Nation to regard any nuclear missile launched from Cuba against any nation in the Western Hemisphere as an attack by the Soviet Union on the United States..."

variants.lower_third: PRESIDENT DEMANDS REMOVAL OF SOVIET MISSILES
PRESIDENT CALLS FOR HALT TO SOVIET BUILDUP

frames.caption: By the next morning, stores in several cities reported shelves cleared of canned food and bottled water.
Not broadcast: that same evening, Robert Kennedy asked the Soviet embassy for a private meeting.
We interrupt this program. The Defense Department has confirmed air strikes against the Soviet missile sites in Cuba.

frames.lower_third: U.S. AIRCRAFT STRIKE MISSILE SITES IN CUBA
frames.caption: The Pentagon will not say how many sites were destroyed. Moscow has not responded.
Across the country, schools ran air-raid drills this afternoon. Some parents kept their children home.
The quarantine of Cuba has been tested for the first time.

frames.lower_third: NAVY STOPS SOVIET SHIP AT QUARANTINE LINE
frames.caption: American sailors have stopped a ship bound for Cuba. Moscow calls the quarantine piracy.
Outside the White House, two crowds tonight, one asking for talks and one asking for an invasion.
American troops are in Cuba.
The Defense Department calls it a limited operation. Reporters have not been allowed near the beaches.
Civil defense offices report thousands of calls an hour. Most callers ask the same thing: where is the nearest shelter?
An American reconnaissance plane has been shot down over Cuba.

frames.lower_third: U-2 DOWNED; U.S. PLANES STRIKE BACK
frames.caption: The pilot, Major Rudolf Anderson, was killed. Within hours, American planes hit the site that fired.

variants.caption: At dawn, a wider strike began against the missile sites.
Schools stayed open. In many homes, the radio was not turned off all night.

frames.caption: The White House has answered Moscow's offer on the radio.
Soviet missiles out of Cuba, American missiles out of Turkey. In Ankara and Bonn, governments ask why they heard it on the radio.
Republican leaders accuse the President of trading an ally's security under pressure. The election is ten days away.
American and Soviet forces are in combat for the first time since 1945.
Soviet units on the island are fighting back. The Pentagon has stopped giving numbers.
In Europe, the roads into West Berlin are closed. NATO forces are on full alert.
Not broadcast: neither side has used a nuclear weapon. Both sides have them ready.
The Defense Department says air operations over Cuba have ended. No American troops have landed.
Soviet freighters are leaving Cuban ports with U.S. Navy ships alongside. Moscow has not commented on its dead.
The Defense Department says organized resistance in Cuba is ending.
American troops control the missile sites. The weapons will be shipped out under guard.
The news this morning did not come from Moscow.

frames.lower_third: CASTRO: CUBA WILL SEND THE WEAPONS HOME
frames.caption: Fidel Castro says Cuba will return the Soviet weapons itself, in exchange for a guarantee against invasion. Moscow has not commented.
Soviet freighters left Mariel this week. The Pentagon calls it routine traffic.
Not broadcast: there were missiles in Cuba, and now there are not. The country never found out.
Radio Moscow announced this morning that the missiles will be dismantled and shipped home. In Washington, officials speak of firmness.
The United States has pledged not to invade Cuba. Asked whether anything else was offered, the White House says no.
Not broadcast: the Jupiter missiles in Turkey will be removed within months. If Moscow ever says so in public, the deal is off.
Radio Moscow confirms the deal: missiles out of Cuba, missiles out of Turkey.
The world has stepped back from the edge. The State Department says the Jupiters were obsolete anyway.
Radio Moscow says the missiles will be dismantled and shipped home.
Reconnaissance flights show crates on the docks. Washington cannot say what is still on the island.
The bombing has stopped. The roads into West Berlin remain closed.
The White House says only that talks will continue. It will not say what it offered.
Not broadcast: the price of the ceasefire is being negotiated over Berlin.
The roads into West Berlin are closed. The first cargo planes of a new airlift landed tonight.
The Pentagon says the missile sites in Cuba no longer exist. Asked about Berlin, it referred questions to the State Department.
Moscow has not announced a withdrawal. The missiles are still in Cuba.

variants.caption: The President promised the country the missiles would go. Republican candidates are quoting his speech back to him.
Washington says the situation is under control. Congressional leaders are asking for a briefing.
